newsitem.title: UK: UK police to question woman caught with boy, 14.
newsitem.headline: UK police to question woman caught with boy, 14.

text.p: British police flew to Florida on Friday to interview a woman who has been charged with "lewd and lascivious behaviour" after she was caught with her neighbour's 14-year-old son in an apparent elopement from England.

Tracey Lee Whalin, 33, from Nottingham, was charged in a Monroe County, Florida court on Thursday after she and teenager Sean Kinsella were found together in a condominium in the Florida Keys, a seaside resort area.
British police said they want to speak to Kinsella before meeting U.S. prosecutors on Monday to discuss transferring Whalin back to England.

"Our officers will speak with local police and prosecutors. If they agree to return Mrs Whalin to this country she will be interviewed and one of the charges she may face is abduction," a police spokesman told The Independent newspaper.
"Obviously, until she has been interviewed over here, it is impossible to say exactly what charges she may or may not face."
Whalin and Kinsella, the soccer-playing best friend of her son, disappeared from England 12 days ago. When Kinsella opened the condominium door for the police, he said: "She's not decent right now."
British police had been seeking the couple since Whalin allegedly left her husband, took $5,000 out of the bank and drove off with Kinsella under the pretense of taking him to school.
They are believed to have flown to Orlando, Florida and visited Disney World before taking a bus to Tavernier, a community in the Keys, according to police investigators.
Authorities say Kinsella told them he and Whalin were romantically involved but refused to say if they had a physical relationship.
The boy had called his mother from Tavernier to say he was still in England and all was well.
Whalin is in custody pending bail of $175,000. She will appear in the Florida court again on August 12.
